cases.summary: GPU 6 and 7 show sustained high NVLink CRC errors (4235/4220 increase) with XID 74, while neighboring GPUs show 0 CRC errors. Temperatures and power are elevated only on GPU 7 (70°C max, 598W), but the primary fault signal is NVLink CRC counters, matching runbook symptoms. No thermal_residual or power_fault signals observed. XID 74 confirms NVLink error. Node should be drained to prevent job slowdowns.
cases.rationale: NVLink degradation causes job slowdowns and requires node drainage per runbook remediation. Resetting GPUs or replacing parts is recommended after drainage, but drainage is the immediate action to prevent performance impact.

cases.summary: GPU 3 and 5 showed elevated power (322W/323W), temp (max 71°C/72°C), and utilization (40%) during the incident window, but these metrics are fully explained by their power draw (no thermal_residual, no ECC/PCIe/NVLink errors, power limit at default 700W). Neighboring GPUs (e.g., GPU 7 at 674W/96% util) showed similar scaling, confirming a workload shift rather than hardware fault. Runbook rb-007-noisy-neighbor-triage confirms this pattern.
cases.rationale: Workload shift confirmed: no hardware action required. The telemetry aligns with the detector's `[workload_shift]` signal (rb-022-detector-alerts-guide#model-alerts), and the runbook (rb-007-noisy-neighbor-triage#what-to-do) explicitly states no action is needed for confirmed workload shifts.

cases.summary: All 8 GPUs on ci923342-a100-node-01 show enforced power limits at 240W (below nominal 400W), with no thermal residuals, ECC/PCIe/NVLink errors, or BMC logs indicating a fault. This matches the telemetry signature of a power fault (PSU redundancy loss), confirmed by the runbook's power capping policy (rb-015-power-capping-policy#when-nodes-get-capped). GPU 6's low utilization is unrelated (idle GPU), not a fault signal.
cases.rationale: Power fault detected (enforced power limit < default), requiring node-level investigation. BMC logs missing but telemetry confirms power capping policy trigger; drain_node is required before hardware checks.

cases.summary: GPU 4 on ci923342-h100-node-01 shows accelerating correctable ECC errors (SBE) from 5 to 50 per 30 minutes, followed by retired pages (1 page) and an uncorrectable error (XID 48, DBE). Telemetry confirms no thermal runaway (temp max 46°C), power limit at default (700W), and low PCIe replay (2). This matches runbook symptoms for ecc_degradation: rising SBE rate, retired pages, and XID 48. The GPU requires replacement.
cases.rationale: Runbook diagnosis confirms repeated ECC degradation on a single GPU requires RMA. XID 48 (DBE) and retired pages indicate hardware failure; replacement is the remediation for uncorrectable errors.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on node ci923342-a100-node-02 shows steadily increasing PCIe replay counters (from 1 to 3465 in 30 minutes) with no thermal or power anomalies. Temperatures (60-65°C) and power limits (400W default) are normal, ruling out thermal_runaway or power_fault. No BMC logs or ECC errors found. Runbook confirms this symptom pattern matches PCIe link degradation.
cases.rationale: PCIe replay counter increased from 129 to 3465 in 30 minutes (per evidence). Runbook states: 'Replays without errors are not urgent, but they often come before a GPU falls off the bus. Schedule a drain.' Remediation requires reseating the GPU/cable during maintenance.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on ci923342-h100-node-04 shows accelerating correctable ECC errors (SBE) rising from 6 to 57 in 30-min bursts, culminating in an uncorrectable DBE error (XID 48) and 1 retired page. Power limit remains at default (700W), temperatures are normal (65-69°C), and no thermal or power faults observed. This matches the runbook's escalation criteria for ecc_degradation (sev1 on DBE/XID 48).
cases.rationale: Runbook diagnosis confirms hardware failure in GPU memory (H100) due to escalating ECC errors. Repeated incidents on the same GPU (evidenced by retired pages and DBE) require RMA. No other fault signals (thermal/power) present, so not noisy_neighbor or power_fault.

cases.summary: GPU 6 fell off the bus (XID 79) with PCIe fatal error in BMC logs. Telemetry shows GPU 6 stopped reporting (0% utilization, 55W power, 30.5°C temp) while all other GPUs on the node operate normally (376-381W power, 65°C temps). Thermal history rules out overheating (GPU 6 is cooler than neighbors). No ECC/PCIe replay errors on other GPUs. Matches runbook symptoms for XID 79: GPU disappearance, PCIe fatal error, and XID 79 event.
cases.rationale: GPU fell off the bus (XID 79) requires node drain before rebooting. Per runbook remediation: 'Drain the node (rb-009-node-drain). The GPU can't be recovered while the OS is running.'

cases.summary: GPU 0 and 2 showed sustained thermal residuals (+12.9-17.9°C above predicted temperature based on power draw) and thermal throttling (2-3 samples per minute at 87-88°C), while neighboring GPUs (1,3,4) remained cool (30-39°C) with no power limit changes (700W default). No BMC/XID logs were found, but telemetry matches thermal runaway symptoms: GPU temperatures exceeding predictions without power faults or ECC errors. GPU 0 had the highest thermal residual (+17.9°C) and was prioritized for reset.
cases.rationale: Thermal runaway confirmed by thermal_residual telemetry and throttling. Runbook symptoms section states 'GPU running more than about 5 C hotter than its power draw predicts is the earliest telemetry sign'. Action: reset GPU 0 to clear transient thermal state before replacement if recurring.

cases.summary: Thermal runaway caused by a failed chassis fan (FAN1 at 0 RPM), confirmed by BMC log entry (ev-8) and thermal_residual alerts (ev-10, ev-15). GPUs 0 and 1 showed 12-16°C hotter than predicted by power draw, with throttling (ev-18, ev-21) while neighboring GPUs (2-3, 4, 6-7) remained cool. GPU 5's initial workload shift (ev-0-2) was a red herring; the root cause is hardware failure, not workload change.
cases.rationale: Hardware fan failure caused thermal runaway on GPUs 0 and 1. Node must be drained for hardware inspection and fan replacement (per runbook remediation for thermal runaway).

cases.summary: All 8 GPUs on node ci923342-a100-node-01 have enforced power limits reduced to 240W (below nominal 400W), with no thermal issues, ECC errors, or BMC logs indicating a fault. Telemetry shows normal temperatures (30-33°C), low utilization (0% avg), and zero error counters. This matches the symptom of a power fault (PSU redundancy loss) as described in runbook rb-015-power-capping-policy#rules, where power capping occurs automatically after PSU fault. The absence of BMC logs does not negate the telemetry evidence, as BMC logs are often missing for transient faults.
cases.rationale: Power capping due to PSU fault requires hardware investigation. Drain the node to prevent further workloads from being affected while the BMC power policy is checked (per rb-015-power-capping-policy#rules).
